input_tensor.description: The tensor to reduce. Should have numeric type.

axis.description: The dimensions to reduce. If `None` (the default), reduces all dimensions. Must be in the range `[-rank(input_tensor), rank(input_tensor))`.
constraints: must be in the range [-rank(input_tensor), rank(input_tensor))
If axis is None, all dimensions are reduced.
Unless keepdims is true, the rank of the tensor is reduced by 1 for each entry in axis, which must be unique.

keepdims.description: If true, retains reduced dimensions with length 1.
constraints: Unless keepdims is true, the rank of the tensor is reduced by 1 for each entry in axis, which must be unique.
If keepdims is true, the reduced dimensions are retained with length 1.

output.description: The reduced tensor. @compatibility(numpy) Equivalent to np.mean Please note that `np.mean` has a `dtype` parameter that could be used to specify the output type. By default this is `dtype=float64`. On the other hand, `tf.reduce_mean` has an aggressive type inference from `input_tensor`, for example: >>> x = tf.constant([1, 0, 1, 0]) >>> tf.reduce_mean(x) <tf.Tensor: shape=(), dtype=int32, numpy=0> >>> y = tf.constant([1., 0., 1., 0.]) >>> tf.reduce_mean(y) <tf.Tensor: shape=(), dtype=float32, numpy=0.5> @end_compatibility

constraints: Unless keepdims is true, the rank of the tensor is reduced by 1 for each entry in axis, which must be unique.
